key_insight: Standard LoRA factor gradients cannot reveal task-relevant directions normal to the low-rank manifold, so optimizing current capacity alone cannot determine when more rank is needed.
engineering_relevance: Geometry-guided rank expansion can improve fine-tuning performance while reducing trainable parameter budgets.
method: Optimize existing degrees of freedom using tangent-space information.
Estimate the normal spectrum matrix-free to identify valuable rank expansions.
Add leading normal singular directions with task-induced geometric initialization.
evidence_signal: Across evaluated language and vision settings, GEAR reports the best average performance; on LLaMA3-8B, average commonsense score rises from 86.61 to 88.45 while trainable parameters fall from 42.0M to 14.4M.
watch_item: Optimal rank expansion is justified under a local quadratic model; the abstract does not quantify the runtime overhead of normal-spectrum estimation.
paper_title: From What Is Used to What Is Missing: Rethinking Dynamic Rank in LoRA
